text:
Search found related semantic–collaborative alignment work, but no verified exact match for BERT4Rec with a title/description encoder jointly trained from random initialization. RecSys 2024’s [The Elephant in the Room](https://github.com/777pomingzi/Rethinking-PLM-in-RS) initializes BERT4Rec item embeddings using a behavior-tuned pretrained language model; its “from scratch” reproduction still starts with Longformer weights. [DenseRec (2025)](https://earl-workshop.github.io/pdf/recsys2025-workshops_paper_167.pdf) learns a projection between pretrained content embeddings and ID embeddings, reporting improvements for SASRec, especially with unseen history items. It cautions that semantic similarity can obscure differences in item appeal. [SISA-Rec (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11168) combines gated ID/text fusion, semantic attention and contrastive alignment, but does not establish the requested randomly initialized BERT4Rec setup.

A constraint-compatible research hypothesis is therefore a small, randomly initialized token embedding plus mean-pooling or CNN encoder over available titles/descriptions, fused residually with item IDs inside one BERT4Rec network. Train jointly through masked-item prediction; optionally test a weak item-level ID–text alignment loss. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated gains from the cited papers. Preserve item-specific ID capacity, suppress text contributions when metadata is absent, and use text dropout to test robustness. Compare against matched ID-only controls under identical training and validation settings; ablate titles versus descriptions and alignment, and inspect missing-text and item-frequency groups. Mask target metadata alongside target IDs to prevent leakage, retain appended-mask inference, and select using the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10. Textual resemblance alone establishes neither ownership nor product compatibility.
